clue.text: Port, as drunk at the end of second degree

indicators.note: says the rearranged pair is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second
MBA is the Master of Business Administration degree

indicators.note: drunk means the word as staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: A glass of port, sipped while finishing a second degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink being drunk, but it is the definition; 'drunk' is the anagram signal and 'at the end of' places that pair last.
explanation.definitionFit: Mombasa is a major seaport city on the Kenyan coast.

clue.text: Bird poo with a crust cracks

indicators.note: the words with a crust split the poo open and sit in the crack

parts.note: muck is dung or excrement
and means together with
a rind is the hard outer crust of cheese or fruit

explanation.surface: Bird droppings, crusted over and cracking as they dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a crust' gives three pieces, and 'cracks' means they break into the poo, sitting just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin duck is a brightly coloured East Asian species of waterfowl.

clue.text: Growth of medicine's beginning to get rid of pain

indicators.note: beginning asks for only the opening letter of medicine's

parts.note: to oust is to get rid of or expel
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A growing lump that only began to go once the medicine took the pain away.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair on the upper lip is something a man grows, so it is fairly called a growth.

clue.text: Silly sailor's irrational

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; the apostrophe S is read as is, a link
a surd is an irrational number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A daft sailor is being unreasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' looks like a plain adjective but works as the maths noun: a surd is a root that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is ridiculous or foolish, a close synonym of silly.

clue.text: Effect of current and temperature on charged particle

parts.note: AC is alternating current
T is the standard symbol for temperature
an ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule

explanation.surface: A physics question on how current and heat act on a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: The action of something is its effect or influence, as in the action of a drug.

clue.text: Fellow confronted over coffee

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the pieces over, reading them backwards

parts.note: faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A man was challenged over a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses F + FACED (FFACED) to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaff is coffee from which the caffeine has been removed.

clue.text: Parisian and a famous revolutionary set off

indicators.note: revolutionary tells us the pieces turn right round, reading backwards

parts.note: et is French for and, as a Parisian would say it
noted means famous

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a celebrated revolutionary leader set out together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses ETANOTED. 'a famous revolutionary' wants to be a person such as Che, but 'revolutionary' is only the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to cause it to explode, which is what detonate means.

clue.text: Spooner's watch arrived in Newmarket, perhaps

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a guard is a watch, someone keeping lookout
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A watchman turned up at Newmarket, perhaps at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket looks like the Suffolk town famous for horse racing, but it is also the name of a card game; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a gambling game played with cards, so it is one example of the category.

clue.text: Argument of rowing crew leader is baseless

indicators.note: the leading letter, a capital E, loses its bottom stroke and becomes a capital F

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers

explanation.surface: A row breaks out because the crew's stroke has no grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Visual trick: a capital E with its base bar removed looks like an F, so EIGHT becomes the answer. 'rowing' also suggests a row, an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight can be a heated quarrel or dispute, not only a physical brawl.

clue.text: Religious women hiding love for sex and drugs and rock and roll?

definitions.text: sex and drugs and rock and roll?
definitions.note: a plural noun: each of these words belongs to a class of words

indicators.note: the women keep the love hidden inside them

parts.note: nuns are women in religious orders
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Nuns secretly giving up love in favour of the rock-star lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is grammatical: sex, drugs, rock and roll are all naming words. The question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the listed words is a naming word in grammar, so together they are examples of that part of speech.

clue.text: Teacher's function is to express irritation over fashion

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in annoyance
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
a rage is a craze or fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A teacher's job seems to be tutting at the latest trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about' but stands for O, a cricket over: a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorage is the work or office of a tutor, so it is the role a teacher carries out.

clue.text: Shops German chemist runs, but runs secretly

parts.note: Fritz Haber was the German chemist behind the synthesis of ammonia

indicators.note: secretly says the second runs is tucked out of sight inside the first

parts.note: dashes means runs quickly
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A German scientist dashes about, but on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secretly' hides R inside DASHES to make DASHERS. 'Shops' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Haberdashers are shops selling sewing goods such as buttons, ribbon and thread; in Britain the word names the shop as well as the shopkeeper.

clue.text: PM wanting nobody to finish early

parts.note: after means seeking or wanting, as in being after something

indicators.note: the word for nobody stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: no one means nobody

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister hoping that nobody leaves work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish early' cuts the last letter from NOONE to leave NOON. 'PM' wants to be the Prime Minister; it is post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, marks the hours after midday, the later half of the day.

clue.text: Must leave dry area

parts.note: to go is to leave
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: An order to get out of an arid region.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotta is an informal contraction of got to, meaning have to, an obligation.

clue.text: Desire to marry, wanting first husband

indicators.note: wanting means lacking; the leading letter is the one that goes

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone longing to wed, though first they need a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Mark religious festival on the radio in a rush

parts.note: a stamp is a mark made by pressing

indicators.note: on the radio signals words heard rather than seen

parts.note: Eid is the Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan, among others

explanation.surface: Celebrating a religious festival, broadcast live in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' turns EID into the matching sound written EDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of a herd or crowd.

clue.text: Choose staff to meet judge, at last, one on the circuit

parts.note: to elect is to choose
a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of judge

explanation.surface: Picking someone to join a judge who rides the court circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuit' suggests a circuit judge travelling between courts, but here it is an electrical circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves part of an electrical circuit.

clue.text: Trump unhinged, essentially. Pence? Just a fraction

parts.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind

indicators.note: essentially asks for the core, the central letters of unhinged

explanation.surface: Donald Trump unhinged, and Mike Pence only a fraction of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' and 'Pence' pose as US politicians: trump is British slang for passing wind, and pence the British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, so just a fraction of pence.

clue.text: State part of trade law, a rebuttal

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A government puts forward part of a rebuttal of trade law.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty United States, the first to ratify the constitution.

clue.text: Craftsman irked me terribly, concealing answer

indicators.note: the jumbled words conceal the answer letter within them
terribly suggests the words irked me are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A craftsman annoyed me badly by keeping the answer to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges IRKEDME into DIEMKER, and 'concealing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diemaker is a skilled worker who makes the dies used for stamping or cutting metal.

clue.text: Twist in plot around November

indicators.note: the plot goes around the November letter

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A plot twist arriving in November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a story, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bend is a curve or twist in a road, river or wire.

clue.text: Lack of interest, of course, that always stifles

indicators.note: stifles means smothers; the word for always wraps right round the course

parts.note: ay or aye is an old or Scots word for always
a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: A boring course that always kills enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a lack of enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: Old Republican is supported by prayer

parts.note: on means resting on or supported by

explanation.surface: An elderly Republican kept going by prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the pieces stack so that ON sits beneath and supports the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an archaic, literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: Talk about new song

indicators.note: the talk goes about, around, the new letter

parts.note: chat is talk

explanation.surface: A discussion about a newly released song.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a simple repeated song or melody, as in plainsong or football chants.

clue.text: Man perhaps following advanced ecclesiastical route?

indicators.note: following says the island comes after the advanced letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, one example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man following an advanced route through the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A church aisle is a passage between pews, a route through a church; the question mark admits the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Papa is appalling traitor, meeting American organisation

indicators.note: appalling suggests the word papa is mangled into a new order

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer
US means American

explanation.surface: Dad turns out to be a dreadful traitor working with an American agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges PAPA into APPA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatus is the structure or machinery of an organisation, as in the state apparatus.

clue.text: Ambitious partisan on the move

indicators.note: on the move means the letters of partisan are moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A driven political supporter always on the go.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirant as an adjective describes someone aspiring to a goal, hence ambitious.

clue.text: Stir up Brexit-voting town

definitions.meaning: to rouse or fan a fire or feeling
...-on-Trent, a Staffordshire city, voted heavily to leave the EU in 2016

explanation.surface: Stirring up a town that voted for Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoking a fire means stirring it up; Stoke is short for Stoke-on-Trent, a pro-Leave city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Pathetic threesome, agreed hosts

indicators.note: hosts means the words hold the answer inside them, across their boundary

explanation.surface: A sad trio agree to play host.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or paltry, so a meagre amount is a pathetic one.

clue.text: Pull clock around for New Yorkers, for example

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply

indicators.note: around turns the word for clock backwards

parts.note: to clock is British slang for to notice or see

explanation.surface: Tugging the clock hands round to change time zone for New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' looks like a timepiece but is the British slang verb meaning to notice; 'around' turns that word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is a nickname for Americans, especially Northerners, and New Yorkers are one example.
